newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Dini to talk with Berisha, opposition.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Dini to talk with Berisha, opposition.

text.p: Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini was to fly to Tirana on Sunday for talks with Albanian President Sali Berisha and opposition leaders on how to settle the country's crisis and organise democratic elections.
A Foreign Ministry spokesman said Dini's visit would be a chance to study details of a deal signed by the two sides calling for a national unity government and elections by June.
Italy welcomed the nine-point accord, which also gave rebels holding several towns in the south of the country a week to hand in their weapons. "We see this positively," the spokesman said.
He said Dini was invited to Tirana by the government and the opposition "in consideration of the positive role which Italy has played in seeking to resolve the crisis."
Under the deal, Berisha reversed his earlier refusal to give the Socialist Party, heirs to Albania's communist party, a role in any interim government of national reconciliation.
Dini's brief trip -- the spokesman said he was likely to return in the evening -- follows intensifying mediation efforts by the West as armed rebels tightened their grip on the south.

Berisha extended a 48-hour halt to government military action against the rebels after talks on Saturday with former Austrian chancellor Franz Vranitzky, representing the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE).
The European Union sent Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo to Tirana on Friday on a mediation mission.
Italy says it will repatriate Albanians who crossed the Adriatic to Italy without proper entry papers to seek political asylum. More than 70 have made the trip so far.
